notes.corio:
Parties: Corio Inc. (Delaware corp., 700 Bay Road, Suite 210, Redwood City, CA 94063) as licensee/host; Commerce One, Inc. (Delaware corp., 1600 Rivera Avenue, Walnut Creek, CA 94596) as licensor. Signed by George Kadifa (CEO, Corio, dated 11/5/99) and Mark S. Biestman (VP Worldwide Sales, Commerce One, date blank).

Dates: Effective Date October 29, 1999. Amendment No. 1 dated March 1, 2001. Acceptance testing to finish by Dec 30, 1999; acceptance/rejection notice by Dec 31, 1999. Escrow agreement due within 60 days of Effective Date. Warranty Period 60 days from Effective Date, no later than Dec 31, 1999.

Initial term: Amended to 7 years from the Effective Date (original: 5 years), i.e. to about Oct 29, 2006.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: Auto-renews for successive 1-year periods. Either party can stop it by written notice at least 30 days before the end of the initial term or any 1-year renewal. Amendment keeps the same notice terms.

Termination rights: Material breach uncured 30 days after written notice, then the non-breaching party may terminate on written notice. Immediate termination on notice if either party becomes insolvent or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors. Corio may terminate with refund if the software is not accepted after the third Acceptance Test, or if a warranty breach can't be corrected (refund of prepaid fees). Commerce One may terminate with a pro-rated refund if an infringement claim can't be fixed. No termination for convenience. Survival (11.3): Sections 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14; existing Customers' use rights and Commerce One's support (if Corio keeps paying annual fees) survive.

Governing law: California law (excluding conflicts rules and the 1980 UN CISG). Binding AAA arbitration, one arbitrator, San Francisco County. Loser pays AAA fees; each side bears its own costs.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: License fees, MarketSite.net access fees, maintenance and support fees, and implementation fees are redacted ([*]). Implementation is time and materials, with a redacted cap. Payment terms: license fee due on acceptance; maintenance net 30 from acceptance anniversary; MarketSite access due on acceptance and each anniversary; revenue share quarterly, net 30 after quarter close; services net 30 from milestone invoice. Revenue share: Commerce One pays Corio [*] of MarketSite transaction fees; Corio pays Commerce One [*] of Application Management Revenue, but none for the initial 3,000 Software User licenses (minimum 40 users per Customer). Software Users unlimited. Corio to use commercially reasonable efforts to land 2 Customers within 60 days (non-binding Exhibit D). Fees exclude taxes.

Liability caps and limits: Except for Section 8 indemnity, each party's liability is capped at amounts actually paid by Corio for the relevant transaction in the 12 months before the cause of action is filed. Mutual exclusion of lost profits, procurement costs, and indirect, special or consequential damages (Section 8 excepted). Commerce One indemnifies Corio and its Customers for IP infringement (uncapped); exclusions for use outside Documentation and third-party modifications.

Insurance: none

Audit rights: Corio keeps records for 3 years after the month they cover. Commerce One's independent CPA may inspect once per calendar year on reasonable notice, at Commerce One's cost. Corio pays the audit cost if underpayment exceeds 5%. Shortfalls or overpayments are settled promptly.

Assignment and change of control: Assignment needs prior written consent, including by operation of law. Exception: either party may assign without consent in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all related assets, unless the deal involves a direct competitor of the other party (then consent needed). Violating assignments are void.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: No exclusivity, non-compete or non-solicitation. All licenses are nonexclusive. Commerce One must not contact Corio Customers about non-ASP license sales unless Corio asks, and must refer inbound Customers to Corio. Mutual covenant not to sue over future patents on Developments.

IP ownership and licences: Commerce One owns the Software (licensed, not sold). Corio gets a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except per 14.1) hosting licence for North America, with unlimited sublicensing to Customers (Customer = in the Corio Market Segment, under $1 billion annual revenue). Also royalty-free internal-use and demonstration licences, a resale right for Commerce One software, and a right to seek worldwide expansion at no extra cost (permission not to be unreasonably withheld). No reverse engineering. Developments made solely by Corio belong to Corio unless Commerce One supports them ongoing. Trademark cross-licence during the term.

Source code escrow: Escrow in California, set up within 60 days of the Effective Date; Corio pays the fees. Release if Commerce One dissolves or ceases business, or repeatedly and materially breaches support obligations uncured 60 days after notice. Disputes: 10 business days of officer negotiation, then arbitration. Release licence lets Corio use and modify the source to support the Software for its Customers.

Warranties: Product warranty (performance per Documentation, media, no viruses) for 60 days from the Effective Date, no later than Dec 31, 1999; remedy is fix, replace or refund, and is exclusive. Year 2000 compliance warranty. IP warranty (ownership, no infringement). No-conflict warranty. Implied warranties disclaimed.

Anything else: Acceptance testing allows up to three tests, with Commerce One 15 days to cure after each notice. Support (Exhibit C): 7am–7pm PST Monday–Friday, 24x7 for Priority 1; action plan within 2 hours for P1 and 4 hours for P2. Section 365(n) bankruptcy protection for Corio. Confidentiality is governed by a separate NDA. Corio may subcontract hosting. Force majeure applies. Quarterly product meetings. Amendment controls on conflict.
notes.seaspine:
Parties: Integra LifeSciences Corporation (Delaware corp., 311 Enterprise Drive, Plainsboro, NJ 08536) and PcoMed, LLC (Colorado LLC, 105 S. Sunset Street, Longmont, CO 80501). No amendments provided.

Dates: Effective Date May 15, 2013. Signed by PcoMed May 15, 2013 and by Integra May 29, 2013. First Product Order due within 60 days of Effective Date. Integra accepts within 10 business days of receiving conforming product (Notice of Initial Acceptance, Attachment C).

Initial term: From Effective Date until the date payment is due for Minimum Payment Period 7 (each period is one year, starting on the date in the Notice of Initial Acceptance; payment due 45 days after period ends). Roughly 7 years plus 45 days from acceptance.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: No automatic renewal. Renewal only for periods and terms mutually agreed in writing (§4.2, §12.7). No non-renewal notice needed.

Termination rights: Material breach (§4.3(a)): either party, 60 days' prior written notice, unless cured within the 60 days (or, if not curable in that time, a reasonably acceptable cure plan is presented). Bankruptcy/insolvency (§4.3(b)): immediate termination by written notice. No termination for convenience. On early termination (other than for Integra breach of §5 or §8), Integra may sell inventory and complete in-process components for 18 months (§4.4(c)). Rights cease on expiry. Survival: §§2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 4.4(c), 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12. Separately, PcoMed can convert exclusivity to non-exclusive (see Exclusivity).

Governing law: State of New Jersey (§12.3). Disputes (§12.4): 30 days' senior-officer negotiation, then binding arbitration in Denver, Colorado, 3-person panel (Judicial Arbiter Group, under AAA rules), each party bears its own costs.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Two milestone payments (amounts redacted [***]): first on full execution; second within 30 days after Notice of Initial Acceptance. Royalty ("Fee") of [***]% of Net Sales of Treated and Partially Treated products (separate rates for exclusive and non-exclusive status, redacted), paid quarterly within 45 days after calendar quarter end, in USD. Run Fee: flat redacted amount per run of up to 100 products, due within 30 days of each run; no charge for regulatory runs up to [***] units or four runs. Minimum Payments for Periods 1–7 (amounts redacted), due within 45 days after each period; Integra need only use commercially reasonable efforts, may top up in cash at its sole discretion, and has no liability for a shortfall. PcoMed's sole remedy is conversion to non-exclusive. Offsets: up to [***]% of third-party patent settlement costs against Fees; enforcement costs creditable against Minimum Payments or Fees; reduced Fees still count in full toward Minimums.

Liability caps and limits: No monetary cap. Mutual exclusion of special, consequential, incidental and indirect damages (§9.1), except for breaches of §3.1, §5 and §§8.1–8.2. Indemnities (§10): PcoMed covers IP infringement from its technology, breach of its warranties and product defects tied to its technology; Integra covers infringement from Integra technology, breach of its warranties and defects in Integra Products. Integra's remedy for PcoMed infringement costs is offset against Fees only.

Insurance: none.

Audit rights: PcoMed may have an independent CPA, reasonably acceptable to Integra, inspect Net Sales records once per calendar year, on reasonable notice, at PcoMed's cost. Records are kept per Integra's retention policy. PcoMed reports results within 60 days. Underpayments are paid within 60 days after agreement or final judgment (§6.2).

Assignment and change of control: Consent required for assignment, but not for assignment to an Affiliate (assignor stays liable) or in a merger or sale of all or substantially all of the relevant assets (assignee assumes liabilities) (§12.12). No change-of-control clause.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: PcoMed grants Integra and its Affiliates sole and exclusive worldwide rights in the Field (spinal interbody/intervertebral) (§3.1). Territory is worldwide for 36 months after Notice of Initial Acceptance. Thereafter the PRC may be excluded if Integra has had no sales there; PcoMed must give 60 days' notice before using a third party. Integra may not apply other coatings (except for identification or sterilization) (§3.3). PcoMed may convert to non-exclusive after written notice and a 45-day uncured breach (§3.2). No employee or customer non-solicit. PcoMed rep that a named employee's non-compete (redacted) does not block his employment.

IP ownership and licences: Each party keeps its own technology. Joint inventions belong to PcoMed if primarily about PcoMed Technology, or to Integra if primarily about Integra Products. PcoMed alone files and prosecutes patents at its own cost. No right to manufacture with the technology. Enforcement is split by whether the infringement relates exclusively to PcoMed technology (90-day response period; 6-month follow-up).

Source code escrow: none.

Warranties: Mutual authority and no-conflict reps. PcoMed warrants title, no prior grants, no infringement (knowledge-based) and no litigation; Integra gives similar reps. No time limits stated; no product warranty period.

Anything else: Confidentiality lasts the term plus 20 years (§5.1). Terms of the Agreement are confidential. Force majeure excludes payment obligations. Use of names needs consent. Entire agreement clause. Fee and dollar figures are redacted in the filing.
notes.dynamex:
Parties: Purolator Courier Ltd. ("Purolator") and Parcelway Courier Systems Canada Ltd., a subsidiary of Dynamex Inc. ("Dynamex"). Independent contractors (s.33). Notices to Dynamex go to Dynamex Inc., 2630 Skymark Ave, Suite 610, Mississauga; Purolator at 5995 Avebury Rd, Suite 500, Mississauga.

Dates: Agreement dated 20 Nov 1995 (effective that date). Amendment No. 1 dated 1 June 1997 (illustrative amendment, not a real filing).

Initial term: None fixed; continues indefinitely until terminated (s.2.1).

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: No renewal mechanism (evergreen/indefinite); ended only by termination.

Termination rights:
- Without cause: Amendment replaces 19.1; either party may terminate on twelve (12) months' written notice (original was two (2) years, now superseded).
- Change of control (19.2): the other party may terminate on written prior notice (no period specified).
- Default (17.2): non-defaulting party may terminate on 120 days' written notice, or immediately on written notice for 17.1(g) (more than 3 Monthly Performance Failures in 12 months) and 17.1(h) (breach not cured within 30 days of written notice). Other defaults: insolvency/bankruptcy (petition not dismissed within 60 days), ceasing business, etc. Also may recover monies due and retake property/Freight without notice.
- Immediate termination if Dangerous Goods Training Certificates are not provided (13.2).
- Reputation (41.1): terminate on such notice as it deems appropriate.
- Termination is without prejudice to damages claims (17.3).

Governing law: Ontario; Ontario courts, parties attorn (36.1). Disputes go to arbitration first (condition precedent): single arbitrator appointed within 10 business days, Toronto seat, Arbitration Act, costs shared equally, final and binding (s.39).

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Purolator pays Dynamex Schedule D rates; Dynamex pays Purolator Schedule E rates (schedules not provided). Currency CAD. Invoices twice monthly (15th and last day), net 15 days, delivered within 3 days; interest at CIBC Toronto Main prime on amounts overdue 30+ days. GST zero-rated (interlining). No minimum fees. Commitments: on-time performance at least 90%; each must tender all relevant requests to the other (3.7, 3.8). Penalty: if more than 3 Monthly Performance Failures in 12 months, 5 × (90% − actual) × shipments × the other party's average yield (example $250).

Liability caps and limits: Liability for loss/damage/delay to Freight in its care; capped at the other party's contractual liability to its customers: $4.41/kg or $2.00/lb unless higher value declared (6.3). Mutual indemnity (8.1) even if negligence, but capped at the insurance coverage in s.9 (8.2). Claims paid within 45 days; set-off right (7.1). Dangerous Goods: no liability absent actual prior knowledge.

Insurance: Each party: cargo liability ≥ $100,000 per occurrence; auto/general/property liability ≥ $2,000,000 per occurrence. Other party as additional insured, cross-liability, waiver of subrogation, 30 days' notice of cancellation, annual certificates; subcontractors must carry equivalent.

Audit rights: Performance reports, records and books open to the other party on request (14.1, 14.3); may request validation through a jointly agreed auditor (14.4).

Assignment and change of control: No sale, assignment or subcontracting without prior written consent (23.1). Change of control gives the other party a termination right (19.2).

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: Purolator may not solicit next-day/multi-day freight from Dynamex's existing sameday customers (3.5); Dynamex may not solicit overnight freight from Purolator customers (3.6); no duration stated. Dynamex may not provide sameday service for other next-day carriers (3.9; Alltours exception up to $5,000/month). Similar agreements in Canada/US need consent (3.11). Post-termination non-compete: 6 months after default termination (defaulting party); 12 months after change-of-control termination (party whose control changed). No employee non-solicit.

IP ownership and licences: Each party keeps its trade-marks; use of the other's only with written consent (s.35).

Source code escrow: none

Warranties: Mutual reps on authority, no breach, licences, no material litigation (s.21). No time limits.

Anything else: Confidentiality (s.34) and public announcements by mutual agreement (s.38). Force majeure (s.22). Entire agreement; precedence is Agreement, Schedules, operating plan. Time of the essence. Amendments must be in writing. Schedules A–F not provided.
notes.bnl:
Parties: Virtual Item Processing Systems, Inc. ("VIP"), 2525 NW Expressway, Suite 105, Oklahoma City, OK 73112 (Oklahoma corporation), service provider; Brokers National Life Assurance Company ("BNL"), 7010 Hwy. 71 W., Suite 100, Austin, TX 78735 (Arkansas-domiciled insurer), customer.

Dates: Agreement executed as of May 1, 2006 (Effective Date); signed by VIP May 17, 2006 and BNL May 18, 2006. Amendment No. 1 dated January 15, 2008 (fee change effective Feb 1, 2008).

Initial term: One year from May 1, 2006.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: Auto-renews year to year (Extended Terms) unless either party gives written notice at least 6 months before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Extended Term. If BNL terminates during an Extended Term with under 6 months' notice, it pays a cancellation fee: the greater of (i) Minimum Fee x remaining months, (ii) average monthly billings over the prior 6 months x remaining months, or (iii) $30,000.

Termination rights: No termination for convenience beyond non-renewal notice (6 months). For cause by the non-breaching party: BNL non-payment uncured 30 days after written notice (if BNL disputes a bill and pays the undisputed part, VIP must first offer a meeting before terminating or starting proceedings); other material breach uncured 30 days after written notice; insolvency/bankruptcy/receivership/creditor assignment. On termination, VIP gives BNL data copies, charged at $100/hr programming and $150/hr computer processing. After notice of termination, non-routine services are billed as additional services at Schedule A rates (termination consultation $100/hr, programming $185/hr, computer time $250/hr). BNL must return VIP software and manuals.

Governing law: Amended to Texas law (without regard to conflict of laws); the original said Oklahoma. Disputes go to binding AAA arbitration (3 arbitrators, location set by arbitrators; injunctive relief excepted); court venue is federal or state court in Austin, TX or Oklahoma City, OK. Prevailing party recovers attorneys' fees.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Minimum monthly fee raised from $5,000 to $6,500 effective Feb 1, 2008. Schedule B: $0.305 per policy per month, all BNL plans; fee payable monthly in advance. Extra line $200/month; visual station $25; printer under 299 LPM $25; over 299 LPM $150. Pass-through expenses (forms, phone, travel, postage, COM; some need BNL's prior written approval). Invoices due within 10 days of postmark; late charge 1.5%/month or the legal maximum, whichever is lower. Schedule A hourly rates (consultation $100, junior programmer $85, bank drafts $0.06 each). After month 12, VIP may raise Schedule A rates on 30 days' notice, capped at 10% per year. New products require a written addendum. Base access: 1 line and up to 70 devices. BNL buys its own equipment.

Liability caps and limits: Both parties exclude consequential, special, indirect and punitive damages. Each party's cap is amounts paid in the 12 months before the claim accrued for the specific service (during the first 12 months, the minimum fees for that period). VIP's cap does not cover IP indemnity (8(B)) or data confidentiality (6(A)). BNL's cap does not cover fees under ¶5, 15(a), 15(c) or breach of VIP proprietary rights (¶13). VIP is also not liable for several BNL-caused matters (¶9(G)). Claims must be brought within 2 years of accrual.

Insurance: VIP must maintain property and disaster/business interruption insurance sufficient to replace hardware, software, data and facilities, and provide evidence on written request.

Audit rights: none.

Assignment and change of control: No assignment, subcontracting or delegation without the other party's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld). Binds successors and assigns. Change of control: none.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: none. VIP may serve other clients using the same personnel.

IP ownership and licences: VIP owns the VIP System and enhancements. BNL gets a non-exclusive licence to use it online during the term. BNL Data stays BNL's and is returned on termination. VIP may keep work papers and copies and may use BNL Data only to render services. VIP indemnifies against US patent, trade secret, copyright and trademark infringement claims. BNL consents to VIP naming it as a client in advertising.

Source code escrow: none.

Warranties: VIP warrants that it is duly organized, owns the rights to the System, that the System does not infringe, that services are prompt and workmanlike, and that there is no time-limit lock in the software. All other warranties are disclaimed, including merchantability and fitness. No stated warranty time limits. Backup facility is provided if downtime exceeds 2 consecutive working days. Availability is 7am–5pm Central, Monday–Friday.

Anything else: Indemnities: BNL's for its acts and information; VIP's for its acts and omissions (subject to the caps). Force majeure favors VIP. BNL is solely responsible for security choices. VIP may change the platform on reasonable written notice and bears BNL's resulting costs. Daily offsite backups, with BNL paying its pro rata share of storage. Notices by hand, certified mail (the "three (2) days" deemed-receipt wording is inconsistent) or next-day courier. Entire agreement; amendments must be in writing; no third-party beneficiaries.
notes.verticalnet:
Parties: VerticalNet, Inc. ("VNI") and VerticalNet Enterprises LLC (formerly Tradeum, Inc., d/b/a VerticalNet Solutions; "VNE"), together "Vert"; and Converge, Inc. ("Converge"), Peabody, MA. Amendment No. 1 is between the same parties.

Dates: Agreement entered Oct 9, 2001; effective Oct 1, 2001. Amendment No. 1 entered Apr 1, 2002. Related Amended and Restated Subscription License Agreement (SLA) is effective the same date as the Agreement.

Initial term: Effective Date to March 31, 2003.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: No automatic renewal. Renews only by mutual written agreement, up to three additional one-year Renewal Terms. No notice period for stopping renewal. Renewal minimum fee is set by mutual agreement (4.2). If either Vert party is unwilling to renew on existing terms, that is a "Vert Non-Renewal Election": the non-solicit stops applying to Converge soliciting VNE Service Personnel. A Converge refusal to renew when Vert is willing is a "Converge Non-Renewal Election": any SLA rights apply. Agreement stays in effect past expiry for uncompleted Work Plan obligations.

Termination rights: No termination for convenience. Termination on an Event of Default: (a) insolvency or bankruptcy (involuntary proceedings not dismissed within 60 days) or general assignment for creditors; (b) material breach causing substantial deprivation of benefits, uncured 30 days after written notice (extended to 60 days if curable but not reasonably curable in 30 and cure efforts began in 30 days); (c) Converge non-payment uncured 3 Business Days after written notice. The non-defaulting party must give written termination notice within 10 Business Days after the Event of Default. Automatic termination if the SLA terminates as permitted.

Governing law: US federal law and Commonwealth of Pennsylvania law (conflicts rules excluded); UN CISG excluded. Jury trial waived. Actions must be commenced within 2 years of accrual unless local law forbids.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Original Initial Term Minimum Fee $4,500,000 in 18 equal monthly installments of $250,000. Amendment No. 1 reduces the minimum to $3,750,000 (it controls). It does not change the installment amount or count, so the amended total conflicts with 18 x $250,000; unresolved, flag for a lawyer. First installment is due at execution, then the 1st of each month (Nov 2001 to Mar 2003). Installments are non-refundable. The Quarterly Allocation covers services (Exhibit C: 1,920 estimated hours). Problem Reports and Maintenance Updates are provided even beyond the allocation; Support Requests and Professional Services beyond it are billed at VNE's then-current time charges. Reasonable expenses are reimbursed. Other invoices are monthly in arrears, due 30 days from receipt, with no setoff. Late charge is the lesser of 1.5% per month or the legal maximum. Converge bears sales/use taxes and a withholding gross-up if it reorganizes as a foreign person. Converge pays incremental costs if it overstates severity or the problem is not an Error.

Liability caps and limits: Mutual exclusion of special, incidental, exemplary and consequential damages (including lost profits). Cap: for Enhancements, amounts paid for that Enhancement; for Maintenance and Support, amounts paid in the 3 months before the claim arose. The cap is in addition to fees owed, and VNI and VNE share one collective cap. Exceptions: bodily injury or tangible property damage from willful misconduct or gross negligence, confidentiality breach, and court-awarded interest. Duty to mitigate. Remedies are exclusive: this Agreement versus the SLA, depending on the claim.

Insurance: none.

Audit rights: none.

Assignment and change of control: Either party may assign to an Affiliate. Otherwise prior written consent is needed (not unreasonably withheld). A change of Control (50% or more of voting securities) or a transfer by operation of law is not an assignment.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: Non-exclusive (10.11). No non-compete. Mutual employee and individual contractor non-solicit during the Term plus 1 year. General job postings are allowed. No customer non-solicit.

IP ownership and licences: Vert owns Converge-Requested Enhancements unless a Work Plan or SOW says otherwise, excluding Converge-Independent Materials, Converge Brand Features and Third-Party Materials. Converge grants Vert an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to the Independent and Third-Party Materials. Converge's rights to Updates and Enhancements are as in the SLA. No Source Code obligation except under the SLA.

Source code escrow: none (Source Code only as the SLA provides).

Warranties: Services performed to generally accepted industry standards. Breach must be reported within 90 days of performance. Remedy is repair, replace or re-perform (within 30 days where feasible), as sole remedy. All other warranties are disclaimed.

Anything else: Confidentiality (Section 7), including the Agreement's terms and SEC filing redaction (5 Business Days). Force majeure. Entire agreement with the SLA. Amendments must be in writing. Converge Support Personnel are capped at 7. Severity response times are in Exhibit B (Severity 1: 30 minutes). Notices go to Horsham, PA (Vert) and Peabody, MA (Converge).
